sources.entry: Window Glue - A simple macOS menu bar utility that lets you glue two windows together so that they behave (mostly) as one.

summary.one_liner: Window Glue is a small macOS menu bar utility that glues two windows together so that moving one drags the other, behaving (mostly) as a single unit.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs from the macOS menu bar and is toggled with an "Add Glue" switch that enables snapping mode. When you drag a window near another window, a glow indicator shows snap positions and the dragged window snaps to the target. Shaking a window quickly removes its glue connection. F9 toggles glue mode and Shift+F9 unglues the active window, with shortcuts customizable in Settings. The README says it needs Accessibility permissions to monitor and manage window positions and that no data is collected or transmitted. The interface is localized into 13 languages.
use_cases: keep two macOS windows side by side as one unit
snap windows to each other while dragging
unglue windows with a shake gesture
window management for macOS menu bar
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the Releases page
Mount the DMG and drag Window Glue.app to Applications
Launch and grant Accessibility permissions when prompted
To build from source: clone the repo and open 'Window Glue.xcodeproj' in Xcode 15+
notable: Shake a window to break its glue connection
Glow indicator previews snap positions while dragging
Global keyboard shortcuts F9 and Shift+F9, customizable in Settings
Runs locally with no data collection, per the README
caveats: Requires macOS 13.0 (Ventura) or later and Accessibility permissions
Glued windows lag slightly when the paired window catches up during a drag
Glued windows do not follow automatically to another screen or space; re-gluing requires manually moving the second window
